2.q: what was right in the eyes of Yahweh
2.note: The word “eyes” here represents seeing, and seeing represents judgment. Yahweh saw and approved of Hezekiah’s actions. See how you translated a similar phrase in [2 Chronicles 14:1](ta:14). Alternate translation: [what Yahweh judged to be right] or [what Yahweh considered to be right]

3.note: This is the first month of the Hebrew calendar. It is during the last part of March and the first part April on Western calendars. (See also: [Ordinal Numbers](ta:translate-ordinal))
Here the word “house” represents the temple. Alternate translation: [the temple of Yahweh]

3.q: Hezekiah opened the doors … and repaired them
3.note: Since Hezekiah was king, he may have had his workers do these things. Alternate translation: [Hezekiah ordered his workers to open the doors … and to repair them]

4.note: This refers to the east side of the temple. Alternate translation: [on the east side of the temple]

5.q: carry away the filthiness from the holy place
5.note: The word “filthiness” refers to things that the people had used to worship other gods. The narrator speaks of these things making the temple unacceptable to Yahweh as if they were physically dirty. Alternate translation: [remove the things that defile the holy place] or [remove the things that make the holy place unacceptable to Yahweh]

6.q: what was evil in the sight of Yahweh our God
6.note: The word “sight” here represents judgment. Yahweh saw and did not approve of their ancestors’ actions. Alternate translation: [what Yahweh our God judged to be evil] or [what Yahweh our God considered to be evil]

6.q: turned away their faces from the place where Yahweh lives, and turned their backs on it
6.note: These two phrases share similar meanings. The words “faces” and “backs” represent the people who turned so that their faces were away from the temple and their backs were towards it. Alternate translation: [turned away from the place where Yahweh lives] (See also: [Synecdoche](ta:figs-synecdoche))

6.q: turned away their faces from the place where Yahweh lives, and turned their backs on it
6.note: Rejecting Yahweh and no longer worshiping him is spoken of as if the people had turned away from the temple. Alternate translation: [abandoned Yahweh’s temple and stopped worshiping him]
This refers to the temple. Alternate translation: [the temple where Yahweh lives]

8.q: the wrath of Yahweh had fallen on Judah and Jerusalem
8.note: Here the words “Judah and Jerusalem” refer to the people who live there. Hezekiah speaks of Yahweh being angry with the people and punishing them as if his wrath were an object that fell upon them. Alternate translation: [because Yahweh was angry, he had punished the people of Judah and Jerusalem] (See also: [Metaphor](ta:figs-metaphor))

8.q: an object of terror, of horror, and of scorn
8.note: This can be translated with verbal phrases. Alternate translation: [something that terrifies and horrifies people, and something that people scorn]

8.q: as you can see with your own eyes
8.note: The phrase “with your own eyes” emphasizes that the people can see this for themselves without others having to tell them about it. Alternate translation: [as you can see for yourselves]

9.q: our fathers have fallen by the sword
9.note: The idiom “fallen by the sword” means to die in battle. The word “sword” represents the soldiers, who used swords as their primary weapons. Alternate translation: [our fathers have died in battle] (See also: [Metonymy](ta:figs-metonymy))

10.note: Here the word “heart” represents the thoughts and intentions. Hezekiah speaks of deciding to do something as if that thing were in his heart. Alternate translation: [it is my intention] or [I have decided] (See also: [Metaphor](ta:figs-metaphor))

10.q: his fierce anger may turn away from us
10.note: Hezekiah speaks of Yahweh no longer being angry with them as if Yahweh’s anger were a person who turns away from them. Alternate translation: [he may no longer be angry with us] (See also: [Personification](ta:figs-personification))

11.note: This could mean: (1) “to stand in his presence” or (2) this is an idiom that means to serve a person of high rank. Alternate translation: [to serve him]

12.note:
# General Information:

These verses list the names of the Levites who began to do the work that Hezekiah had ordered them to do. These are all men’s names.
Here the word “arose” is an idiom that means that the Levites began to act. Alternate translation: [the Levites began to work]

15.note: This phrase shows that the king gave his command in obedience to the word of Yahweh. Alternate translation: [in obedience to the word of Yahweh] or [because of what Yahweh had said]

15.q: to cleanse the house of Yahweh
15.note: A place that is fit to be used for God’s purposes is spoken of as if it were physically clean.
Here the word “house” represents the temple. Alternate translation: [the temple of Yahweh]

16.q: the house of Yahweh … the courtyard of the house
16.note: Here the word “house” represents the temple. Alternate translation: [the temple of Yahweh … the courtyard of the temple]

16.q: they brought out all the filth that they found in the temple of Yahweh
16.note: The word “filth” refers to things that the people had used to worship other gods. The narrator speaks of these things making the temple unacceptable to Yahweh as if they were physically dirty. Alternate translation: [they brought out all the defiled things that they found in the temple of Yahweh] or [they brought out all the things that they found in the temple of Yahweh that made it unacceptable to Yahweh]
A small body of water that flows on the east side of Jerusalem. At times it was used as a trash dump.

17.q: the first day of the first month
17.note: This is the first month of the Hebrew calendar. The first day marks the day when Yahweh brought the people out of Egypt. This is near the middle of March on Western calendars. (See also: [Ordinal Numbers](ta:translate-ordinal))

17.q: the eighth day of the month
17.note: This is near the end of March on Western calendars. (See also: [Ordinal Numbers](ta:translate-ordinal))

17.q: they reached the porch of Yahweh
17.note: The phrase “the porch of Yahweh” refers to the porch of the temple. “They reached” means that they began to cleanse this section. Alternate translation: [they had begun to cleanse the porch of Yahweh’s temple] (See also: [Idiom](ta:figs-idiom))

17.q: sixteenth day of the first month
17.note: This is near the beginning of April on Western calendars. (See also: [Ordinal Numbers](ta:translate-ordinal))

18.note: This is a reference to the 12 loaves of bread that were placed in front of the altar. See how you translated this in 2 Chronicles 2:4.

19.note: Alternate translation: [Look at them. You can see for yourself that they are]

20.note: The word “house” represents the temple. Alternate translation: [the temple of Yahweh]

22.q: they killed the bulls, and the priests received the blood
22.note: Alternate translation: [the priests killed the bulls and took the blood]

23.q: they laid their hands on them
23.note: Alternate translation: [the king and people in the assembly laid their hands on them]

24.q: that a burnt offering and a sin offering should be made for all Israel
24.note: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [that the priests should make a burnt offering and a sin offering for all Israel]

25.note: The word “house” represents the temple. Alternate translation: [the temple of Yahweh]
two thin, round metal plates that are hit together to make a loud sound. See how you translated this in 2 Chronicles 5:12.

25.q: arranging them by the command of David, Gad, the king’s seer, and Nathan, the prophet
25.note: The word “command” can be translated with a verbal phrase. Alternate translation: [arranging the Levites as David, Gad, the king’s seer, and Nathan, the prophet had commanded]

25.q: for the command was from Yahweh by means of his prophets
25.note: The word “command” can be translated with a verbal phrase. Alternate translation: [for Yahweh had commanded this through his prophets]

27.q: the song of Yahweh began also
27.note: The phrase “the song of Yahweh” refers to people singing a song to Yahweh. Alternate translation: [the people began to sing a song to Yahweh also]

28.q: until the burnt offering was finished
28.note: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [until the priests finished offering the burnt offering]

29.q: When they had finished the offerings
29.note: Alternate translation: [When the priests had finished the offerings]
The object of worship may be supplied in translation. Alternate translation: [bowed and worshiped Yahweh]

31.note: The word “house” represents the temple. Alternate translation: [the temple of Yahweh]
Here the word “heart” represents the person who was willing. Alternate translation: [who were willing] or [who desired]

32.q: seventy bulls, one hundred rams, and two hundred male lambs

33.q: six hundred oxen and three thousand sheep

34.q: to skin all the burnt offerings
34.note: Alternate translation: [to remove the skins from all the burn offerings]

If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [until they had finished the work]

34.q: until the priests could consecrate themselves
34.note: Since there were some priests who were already consecrated, this implies that more priests consecrated themselves. Alternate translation: [until more of the priests could consecrate themselves]

34.q: had been more careful to consecrate themselves
34.note: There were enough Levites to do this work because they had been careful to consecrate themselves. This implies that the reason that there were not enough priests was because the priests were not careful to consecrate themselves.

35.q: they were performed with the fat of the fellowship offerings
35.note: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [the priests performed the burnt offerings with the fat of the fellowship offerings]

35.q: the service of the house of Yahweh was set in order
35.note: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [Hezekiah set the service of the house of Yahweh in order]
The word “house” represents the temple. Alternate translation: [the temple of Yahweh]
This idiom means that something is organized. Here it refers to the priestly service beginning in the temple again. Alternate translation: [was restored] or [began again]

36.q: the work had been done quickly
36.note: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [the people had done the work quickly]
